BC_description: The `memoize` function from the `async` module no longer caches results when the wrapped asynchronous function returns an error. Previously, if a memoized function called back with an error (i.e., first argument as an error in Node.js-style callbacks), that error result could be cached and rethrown on subsequent calls with the same arguments. Now, errors are explicitly not cached. This means that subsequent calls to the memoized function with the same inputs will re-execute the underlying function instead of returning a cached error. This change affects any usage of `async.memoize` where error states were previously cached and relied upon for consistent behavior across retries.
Adaptation_method:
Before: const memoizedFn = async.memoize(fn); memoizedFn(arg, callback); // if fn(err), it is cached and repeated on next call
After: const memoizedFn = async.memoize(fn); memoizedFn(arg, callback); // if fn(err), it is not cached; next call re-executes fn
